title: Coast Redwood: Ancient Redwoods You Can Visit
meta_description: The tallest tree species on earth drinks fog through its leaves. Colonel Armstrong, in a Sonoma County grove, is roughly 1,400 years old.
intro: The tallest tree species on earth takes a serious share of its water straight out of sea mist, which is why it belongs to the fog belt of the northern Californian coast. There it gets very old: Colonel Armstrong, in the grove a lumberman set aside near Guerneville, is roughly 1,400 years old, and the Parson Jones Tree beside it runs past 94 metres. Europe hands it the rainless summer and none of the fog. So the redwood on Rome's Pincio has stopped at thirty metres, a good height for a Roman tree and a failure for this species, and has gone thick instead. Where the air stays damp the answer is different: Lucca's clears every tower inside the walls except the two you can climb. Most of Europe's went in within a few decades, because seed reached the continent in the 1840s and every ambitious garden wanted one.
